newsitem.title: USA: No new rules expected from U.S. heat oil study - DOE. [CORRECTED 08:10 GMT 26/10]
newsitem.headline: No new rules expected from U.S. heat oil study - DOE. [CORRECTED 08:10 GMT 26/10]

text.p: The Energy Department will work with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the New York Mercantile Exchange to report in April on the influence of the heating oil futures market on heating oil inventories and prices, Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis said Friday.
(Corrects to delete reference to reporting to president in April)
Curtis, speaking to reporters after a meeting with CFTC and NYMEX officials, said no regulatory action was expected from the report.
"We do not anticipate any regulatory response to these markets," he said.
Curtis said the study would look at the role of "non-commercial participants" in magnifying futures price fluctuations and the influence of margins.
He also repeated that the department did not anticipate any government intervention in the physical heating oil markets.
Curtis said the study was only to collect information.

NYMEX president Patrick Thompson, also speaking to reporters, said the report would be a chance to "dispel what may be myths about the marketplace," and said that NYMEX would cooperate fully with the study.
Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary and CFTC chairwoman Brooksley Born also attended the meeting.
The department will report in April on influences of "futures market conditions on inventory management of distillate and heating oil," Curtis said.
(Corrects to delete reference to reporting to Congress and the president in April)

"There was a lot of discussion about price volatility in these markets due to stocks management, and that is a broader issue that we're trying to understand. This is just one element of that understanding," he said.
